## Verdict

wrong

## Bearer

Segment — core-domain/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/domain/race/Segment.kt

## Trigger

None — this is a stored-value gap, not a missing call.

## Today

`Segment.cumulativeMs` is a stored `Long?` field on the domain model.
`buildSegments` (SegmentBuilder.kt) computes it once, as a running sum
of `durationMs`, when the 30 segments are built, and writes it into
each `Segment`. Every reader then takes `segment.cumulativeMs` as
given — `RaceDetailViewModel.buildRow` (app-phone) reads
`segment.cumulativeMs` and the previous segment's `cumulativeMs`
directly to compute the displayed duration and cumulative seconds via
`DurationTruncationService`. No derivation-on-read function exists
anywhere in `:core-domain` that recomputes a cumulative total from a
list of `durationMs` values; the only production code path to a
cumulative value is the field written once at build time.

## Expected

`Segment` carries only `durationMs`; no `cumulativeMs` field is
stored. A cumulative total is derived on read from the segments'
`durationMs` values — the same running-sum rule `buildSegments`
currently applies once, but recomputed each time a cumulative value is
needed, so it can never disagree with the sum of the segment
durations it is derived from. `RaceDetailViewModel.buildRow` and any
other reader obtain the cumulative value from that on-read derivation
instead of a stored field. This requires a derivation function in
`:core-domain` (there is none today, beyond the one-time computation
inside `buildSegments`) that every consumer of a cumulative value
calls in place of `segment.cumulativeMs`.
